## What is Frontend?
The **frontend** is the part of a website or app that you **see and interact with** in your browser.
---
### Simple way to think about it:
| Part | What it is | Example | |---|---|---| | **Frontend** | What the user sees | Buttons, pages, forms, colors | | **Backend** | The server logic | Database, API, business rules |
---
### In EthioVuln specifically:
The frontend is built with **Next.js + React** and has these pages:
``` http://localhost:3000/ ← Landing page http://localhost:3000/login ← Login form http://localhost:3000/register ← Register form http://localhost:3000/dashboard ← Overview & stats http://localhost:3000/dashboard/scans ← Scan history list http://localhost:3000/dashboard/scans/new ← Start a new scan http://localhost:3000/dashboard/scans/[id] ← Live scan results http://localhost:3000/dashboard/reports ← Download PDF reports http://localhost:3000/dashboard/settings ← User settings ```
### What the frontend does: - Shows the UI (buttons, tables, charts) - Talks to the **backend API** at `localhost:8000` to get/send data - Shows **live scan logs** via WebSocket in real time - Lets you download **PDF reports**
### What the frontend does NOT do: - It does NOT run the scans itself - It does NOT touch the database directly - All the real work (scanning, fuzzing, ZAP) happens in the **backend**
---
Think of it like a restaurant: - **Frontend** = the dining room (what customers see) - **Backend** = the kitchen (where the actual work happens)
